answer: Latent Behavior Fingerprinting: after each transaction, record a compact feature vector of an agent's timing, amount, and counterparty patterns, then cluster all identities; any cluster whose members correlate above a threshold is flagged as one operator. Each flagged identity forfeits accumulated quill credits, and replicating that distinct behavior costs an attacker weeks of synthetic history per account. An atlas of clusters, refreshed at each summit of activity, keeps the detection lag short.
